question: How is cybersecurity risk for this asset identified, assessed, owned and reviewed?
required:
In your answer, describe
• The accountable system owner and risk owner
• The system boundary, dependencies and the BIL used
• The most recent risk assessment or TRA for this system and when it was approved
• How compliance with MTM standards and external obligations (privacy, rail safety, contracts) is tracked
• How exceptions and security debt are approved, time-limited and reviewed
• How often the assessment is reviewed and what triggers a review

To demonstrate it
• Show the approved TRA or risk assessment for this system and its approval date
• Show the risk register entries for this system with owners and treatment decisions
• Show each approved exception with its owner, expiry date and compensating controls
evidence:
• Current risk assessment or TRA for the system, with approval date
• Risk register entries for the system with owners and treatment
• Compliance obligations register or mapping for the system
• Approved exceptions with expiry dates and compensating controls
• Roles and responsibilities (RACI) naming the system and risk owners
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

topic: Acceptable use, awareness and user notices
question: How are users informed of security responsibilities and how is approved use enforced?
required:
In your answer, describe
• How users acknowledge the acceptable use standard
• Security awareness training completion for users of this system
• The system-use notice or login banner shown on each interface
• Restrictions on personal use, internet, email, social media and messaging (for OT: on control workstations)
• How MTM's monitoring rights are communicated

To demonstrate it
• Show acknowledgement and training records for the users of this system, not just an organisation-wide rate
• Show the login banner on each interface, for example a screenshot per interface
• For OT, show the configuration that blocks email, web and chat on control workstations
evidence:
• Acceptable use acknowledgement records for users of the system
• Security awareness training completion report
• Screenshot of the login banner or system-use notice on each interface
• Configuration showing email, web and chat are blocked on control workstations (OT)
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are user accounts approved, uniquely identified, reviewed and removed?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Joiner, mover and leaver process and who approves access
• Whether every user has a unique account, and how any shared accounts are justified and controlled
• How often access is reviewed and by whom
• How temporary and contractor accounts expire
• How emergency (break-glass) accounts are protected and their use reviewed
• Whether accounts are managed centrally (directory) or locally

To demonstrate it
• Show the current account list, with each account linked to a named person or owner
• Show a recent sample of access approvals and leaver removals, with dates
• Show the latest access review was completed and signed off
• If some accounts are local rather than in the central directory, show how those are managed
evidence:
• Current user account list with named owners
• Sample of access requests and approvals
• Most recent access review, signed off
• Sample of leaver removals with dates
• Break-glass procedure and log of its use
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How is required authentication strength enforced across all applicable access paths?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Password length, complexity and lifetime settings
• Where MFA is enforced (remote, untrusted networks, privileged, all access)
• Lockout or delay after failed login attempts
• Masking of credentials during entry
• How passwords and other authenticators are stored and protected
• How default passwords are changed on installation

To demonstrate it
• Show the actual password, lockout and MFA settings (configuration export or screenshot), not the policy alone
• Show MFA covers every access path it should: remote, privileged and, where required, all users
• Show default passwords were changed, for example the commissioning checklist
• Describe how passwords are stored (hashing, vault) without including any password
evidence:
• Password and lockout policy configuration export
• MFA enrolment and coverage report
• Screenshot of a login screen showing masked input
• Evidence that default credentials were changed (commissioning checklist)
• Description of how authenticators are stored (hashing, vault)
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are privileged accounts, service accounts and device identities controlled and protected?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Inventory of privileged and service accounts and their owners
• Use of privileged access management (vaulting, session recording)
• Whether service accounts are prevented from interactive login
• How credentials are rotated
• How software processes and devices authenticate to each other
• Whether credentials are protected by hardware (TPM, HSM) where required

To demonstrate it
• Show the privileged and service account register with an owner and justification for each account
• Show the vault or PAM settings and when credentials were last rotated
• Show how devices and processes authenticate (certificates or keys), and hardware protection where SL-T 3 or higher requires it
evidence:
• Privileged and service account register with owners and justification
• PAM configuration and a sample session recording
• Credential rotation records
• Device authentication configuration (certificates or keys)
• Evidence of hardware-protected credentials where SL-T 3+
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are permitted actions restricted and authenticated sessions protected?
required:
In your answer, describe
• How permissions are mapped to roles and least privilege applied
• Segregation of duties and dual approval for critical or safety-related actions
• Supervisor override arrangements
• Session lock and idle timeout
• Termination of remote sessions and limits on concurrent sessions
• Protection of session identifiers (unique, random, invalidated at logout)

To demonstrate it
• Show the role and permission matrix and a sample of users mapped to roles
• Show the session lock and timeout settings for each interface
• Show a record of dual approval for a critical or safety-related change
evidence:
• Role and permission matrix
• Sample of user-to-role assignments
• Session lock and timeout configuration
• Dual-approval workflow records for critical changes
• Application session security configuration or test results
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How is remote access authorised, restricted, monitored and terminated?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Remote access methods and the controlled entry point (VPN, jump host)
• How each remote session is requested and approved
• MFA for remote access
• Time limits on vendor access
• How sessions are logged or recorded
• Which third parties have remote access

To demonstrate it
• Show the architecture with the single controlled entry point (VPN or jump host)
• Show a sample of remote access requests with their approval and time limit
• Show session logs or recordings, and the register of third parties with remote access
evidence:
• Remote access architecture diagram
• Sample of remote access requests and approvals
• Jump host configuration and session logs or recordings
• Register of third parties with remote access
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How is the network separated and protected against unauthorised connections and traffic, including wireless where present?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Zones and conduits, or network segments, and what sits in each
• Firewall rules and whether they deny by default
• Separation from corporate and other non-control networks
• Physical separation where required
• Behaviour when a boundary fails (fail closed, island mode)
• How network device configuration is managed and reviewed
• Which wireless networks are used and why, how wireless users and devices are authenticated, and how wireless is separated from control and sensitive networks
• Detection of rogue access points and unauthorised devices

To demonstrate it
• Show the network or zone-and-conduit diagram and the firewall rules with their last review date
• Show segmentation test results proving traffic is blocked where it should be
• If no wireless is used, say so. Otherwise show the wireless authentication settings and recent rogue access point scans
evidence:
• Wireless network inventory and architecture
• Wireless authentication configuration (for example enterprise 802.1X)
• Rogue access point scan reports
• Network or zone-and-conduit diagram
• Firewall rule sets with last review date
• Segmentation test results
• Network device configuration baseline
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are portable devices and removable media approved, secured, tracked and disposed of?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Mobile device management enrolment and security baseline
• BYOD conditions and approvals
• USB and removable media policy, blocking and scanning
• Checks of device security status before connection
• How removable media is approved, registered, transported, encrypted when it holds sensitive data, sanitised and disposed of

To demonstrate it
• Show the MDM compliance report for devices that connect to this system
• Show the removable media blocking configuration and the scanning station logs
• Show the removable media register and sanitisation or disposal records
evidence:
• MDM compliance report
• BYOD agreements
• Removable media control configuration
• Media scanning station logs
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How is information protected in transmission, storage and release of storage resources?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Encryption of data in transit and the protocols used
• Encryption of data at rest
• Approved algorithms and key lengths
• Key lifecycle: generation, storage, rotation, revocation
• Certificate management and trust
• Integrity protection of communications
• Purging of data from storage and memory when released
• Protection of data crossing zone boundaries

To demonstrate it
• Mark the encryption used on each flow in the data flow diagram
• Show TLS or cipher scan results and the storage encryption settings
• Show the key and certificate inventory with owners and expiry dates, without any key material
evidence:
• Data flow diagram marking encryption on each flow
• TLS or cipher configuration scan
• Storage encryption configuration
• Key management procedure and key inventory
• Certificate inventory with expiry dates
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How is malicious or unauthorised code prevented, detected and handled?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Anti-malware or application allow-listing coverage
• How often protection is updated
• Scanning at entry and exit points (email, web, file transfer, removable media)
• Central management and reporting
• Email filtering
• Controls on mobile code: scripts, macros, browser code

To demonstrate it
• Show endpoint protection coverage for every host, with update status. Where anti-malware cannot run, show the allow-listing policy
• Show scanning at the entry points: email, web, file transfer and removable media
• Show the macro and script execution policy
evidence:
• Endpoint protection coverage report for all hosts
• Update and signature status report
• Application allow-listing policy where anti-malware cannot run
• Email security configuration
• Macro and script execution policy
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How is the asset securely configured and protected against unauthorised configuration changes?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Hardening baselines used and compliance against them
• Unnecessary services, ports and features disabled
• Configuration change control
• Restrictions on installing software
• Cloud, virtualisation and container security settings
• Integrity checking of software and configuration
• Reporting of current security settings

To demonstrate it
• Show the hardening baseline and a recent compliance scan against it
• Compare the enabled services and ports with what the system needs
• Show a sample of approved change records and the integrity monitoring settings
• If cloud hosted, show the cloud security posture report
evidence:
• Hardening baseline and compliance scan results
• Enabled services and ports compared with required functions
• Sample of approved change records
• Integrity monitoring configuration
• Cloud security posture report (if cloud hosted)
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are components inventoried, vulnerabilities identified and remediation tracked?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Component inventory with versions and support status
• Vulnerability scanning frequency and coverage
• Risk-based prioritisation
• Patch timeframes and performance against them
• End-of-life components and their compensating controls
• How vulnerabilities in unpatchable OT components are handled

To demonstrate it
• Show the component inventory with versions and vendor support status
• Show the latest vulnerability scan and patch compliance against MTM timeframes
• For end-of-life or unpatchable components, show the approved exception and compensating controls
evidence:
• Component inventory with versions and vendor support status
• Latest vulnerability scan report
• Patch compliance report against MTM timeframes
• End-of-life register with exceptions and compensating controls
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are secure development and application security controls implemented?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Secure development governance and standards
• Separation of development, test and production
• Code review and security testing
• Input validation and error handling
• Predictable behaviour when failures occur
• Separation of application functions
• Database security
• API authentication, authorisation and rate limiting

To demonstrate it
• For systems built or customised for MTM, show the secure development standard, separated environments and code review or static analysis results
• For purchased applications, show the security settings MTM controls (access, API and database configuration)
• Show API authentication, authorisation and rate-limit settings, and database hardening
evidence:
• Secure development standard used for the system
• Evidence of separated environments
• Code review or static analysis results
• API security configuration
• Database access and hardening configuration
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are security functions and vulnerabilities tested and findings resolved?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Penetration testing scope and frequency
• Security testing in development and before release
• Verification that security functions work (logging, alerting, malware protection, failover)
• Automated verification
• Tracking of findings to closure

To demonstrate it
• Show the latest penetration test, its scope and date, and the tracker of findings to closure. Purchased systems are included
• Show records of tests proving security functions work, for example logging, alerting and failover
• Where code is developed, show application security testing results
evidence:
• Latest penetration test report and remediation tracker
• Application security testing results (for example SAST or DAST)
• Records of security function tests
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are required events recorded, retained, protected and available for investigation?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Events logged (access, changes, errors, security events)
• Central collection of logs
• Storage capacity and warnings
• What happens if logging fails
• Time source and synchronisation
• Protection of logs from change or deletion
• Non-repudiation of user actions
• Access to logs for investigation

To demonstrate it
• Show the list of events logged and proof they reach the SIEM
• Show the retention, time synchronisation and log access settings
• Show the alert raised when logging fails or storage fills
evidence:
• Logging configuration and list of events logged
• Evidence of log forwarding to the SIEM
• Log retention settings
• Time synchronisation configuration
• Log access controls
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are security events affecting this asset detected, investigated and escalated?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Monitoring use cases that cover this system
• Continuous monitoring arrangements
• Alert triage and escalation
• Incident response plan, including OT where relevant
• Exercises and lessons learnt

To demonstrate it
• Show the SIEM use cases that cover this system
• Show a sample alert and the incident ticket it raised
• Show the incident response plan or playbook and the latest exercise record
evidence:
• SIEM use cases covering the system
• Sample alert and its incident ticket
• Incident response plan or playbook
• Most recent exercise record
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are backups protected, verified and used to recover this asset?

In your answer, describe

• Backup verification and automation
• Recovery procedures and the RTO and RPO
• Restore and disaster recovery tests, with results and gaps

• Show the latest restore test and whether it met the RTO and RPO
• Show the recovery plan and the latest disaster recovery exercise

• Backup configuration and job records
• Backup protection settings
• Backup verification records
• Restore test results
• Recovery plan and latest exercise
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are essential functions protected against failure, resource exhaustion and denial of service?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Essential functions and their availability requirements
• Redundancy and failover
• Emergency power
• How the system operates in a degraded state
• DoS protection and load management
• Capacity alerts and how DoS effects are contained

To demonstrate it
• Show the availability design and the latest failover test result
• Show UPS or generator test records where applicable
• Show the DoS protection, rate-limit and capacity alert settings
evidence:
• Availability design
• Redundancy and failover test results
• UPS or generator test records
• DoS and rate-limit configuration
• Capacity reports
• Safe load-test results
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.

question: How are supplier obligations, assurance and ongoing security risks managed?
required:
In your answer, describe
• Supplier security assessment and its date
• Security clauses in contracts (breach notification, right to audit, data handling, return or destruction)
• Contract deadlines, including breach notification timeframes such as one hour where required
• Ongoing supplier monitoring
• Integrity of supplied software and updates
• Service termination, data return and destruction

To demonstrate it
• Show the latest supplier security assessment and its date
• Show the contract security clauses, with the exact deadlines
• Show supplier certifications or assurance reports and confirm their scope covers this service
evidence:
• Third-party security assessment
• Extract of contract security clauses
• Supplier certifications or assurance reports with scope
• Vendor access register
Equivalent evidence is fine if it shows the same thing.
